what_it_does: This paper describes a radio transceiver using impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB)—a wireless technology that sends very short pulses across a wide spectrum to communicate at short distances with low power. The challenge is supporting multiple channels (5 through 12) to avoid interference in the crowded 6 GHz band while keeping cost low through shared antennas. Previous designs used external RF switches or antennas, which introduced signal loss and reduced receiver sensitivity. This paper integrates the antenna-switching circuits directly onto the chip using CMOS transistors, minimizing signal loss and reducing component count.
